ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Don't Let Anger Be Your Boss

fullPassage:
Do you ever find yourself suddenly feeling angry? One moment you're fine, and the next moment you're slamming doors or rolling your eyes at your parents. Some people may think you just have a bad attitude or are getting too upset about a small problem. However, these feelings don't simply come from stress about everyday life.

As a teenager, you are going through a lot of changes. You are developing your identity and trying to become independent. At the same time, your brain is still growing and is not yet fully developed. The part of your brain that controls emotions is more active than the part that controls rational thinking. On top of that, hormones can make your emotions feel more intense than they really are. All of these factors can contribute to feelings of anger.

Getting to Know Your Anger

Anger is a natural emotion, and it is not always a bad thing. In fact, anger can be a useful tool. It can tell you when something is wrong or when you are being treated unfairly. The key is to learn how to manage your anger in a productive way so that it does not control you.

Questions to Ask Yourself

When you feel angry, it can be helpful to ask yourself some questions. Why am I feeling this way? Is my anger justified? Am I overreacting? What is the best way to handle this situation? Is there another way to look at this? What would I tell a friend in the same situation? These questions can help you step back and think more clearly before you act.

First Aid to Calm Yourself Down

When anger hits, your body reacts physically. Your heart rate increases, your face becomes flushed, and you may find yourself clenching your fists. These are signs that your body is preparing for a fight. But fighting is rarely the answer. Instead, try some first aid techniques to calm yourself down. Take deep breaths. Count to ten slowly. Walk away from the situation for a few minutes. Drink a glass of cold water. These simple actions can help bring your body back to a calm state.

Finding Proper Coping Skills

Once you have calmed down, it is important to find healthy ways to deal with your anger. Some people find it helpful to go for a walk or exercise. Others prefer to express their feelings through drawing or writing in a journal. Talking to someone you trust, like a friend, family member, or counselor, can also be very helpful. Another useful skill is problem-solving. Instead of focusing on how angry you feel, try to focus on finding a solution to the problem that caused your anger.

Conclusion

Remember, everyone gets angry sometimes. It is a normal part of being human. But you have the power to choose how you respond to your anger. Don't let anger be your boss. Instead, learn to be the boss of your feelings. By understanding your anger, asking the right questions, calming yourself down, and finding proper coping skills, you can take control of your emotions and handle difficult situations in a healthier way.

questions.passage: As a teenager, you are going through a lot of changes. You are developing your (A)[identity / anonymity] and trying to become independent. At the same time, your brain is still growing and is not yet fully developed. The part of your brain that controls emotions is more (B)[active / inactive] than the part that controls rational thinking. On top of that, hormones can make your emotions feel more (C)[intense / mild] than they really are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 정체성(identity)을 발달시키고, 감정 통제 부분이 더 활발(active)하며, 호르몬이 감정을 더 강렬(intense)하게 느끼게 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① identity — active — intense: 원문 일치
❌ ② anonymity(익명성): identity의 반의어
❌ ③ inactive(비활동적인): active의 반의어
❌ ④ mild(약한): intense의 반의어
det.tip: identity(정체성) ↔ anonymity(익명성), active(활발한) ↔ inactive(비활동적인), intense(강렬한) ↔ mild(약한)

questions.passage: Anger is a (A)[natural / artificial] emotion, and it is not always a bad thing. In fact, anger can be a useful tool. It can tell you when something is wrong or when you are being treated (B)[unfairly / fairly]. The key is to learn how to manage your anger in a (C)[productive / destructive] way so that it does not control you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 분노는 자연스러운(natural) 감정이고, 부당하게(unfairly) 대우받을 때를 알려주며, 생산적(productive) 방식으로 관리해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ natural — unfairly — productive: 원문 일치
❌ ① artificial(인공적인): natural의 반의어
❌ ② fairly(공정하게): unfairly의 반의어
❌ ④ destructive(파괴적인): productive의 반의어
det.tip: natural(자연스러운) ↔ artificial(인공적인), unfairly(부당하게) ↔ fairly(공정하게)

questions.passage: Once you have calmed down, it is important to find healthy ways to deal with your anger. Some people find it helpful to go for a walk or exercise. Others prefer to (A)[express / suppress] their feelings through drawing or writing in a journal. Talking to someone you (B)[trust / distrust], like a friend, family member, or counselor, can also be very helpful. Another useful skill is (C)[problem-solving / problem-avoiding].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 감정을 표현(express)하고, 신뢰하는(trust) 사람에게 이야기하며, 문제 해결(problem-solving)이 유용하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② express — trust — problem-solving: 원문 일치
❌ ① suppress(억누르다): express의 반의어
❌ ③ distrust(불신하다): trust의 반의어
❌ ④ problem-avoiding(문제 회피): problem-solving의 반의어
det.tip: express(표현하다) ↔ suppress(억누르다), trust(신뢰하다) ↔ distrust(불신하다)

questions.passage: Do you ever find yourself suddenly feeling angry? One moment you're fine, and the next moment you're slamming doors or rolling your eyes at your parents. Some people may think you just have a bad <u>① attitude</u> or are getting too <u>② upset</u> about a small problem. However, these feelings don't <u>③ simply</u> come from stress about <u>④ unusual</u> life.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 '일상적인(everyday)' 삶인데, '특이한(unusual)'으로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① attitude: 태도, 원문 일치
✅ ② upset: 속상한, 원문 일치
✅ ③ simply: 단순히, 원문 일치
❌ ④ unusual(특이한) → everyday(일상적인): 반의어로 교체됨
det.tip: everyday(일상적인) ↔ unusual(특이한). 이 감정들은 일상적 스트레스에서만 오는 것이 아니다.

questions.passage: When anger hits, your body reacts physically. Your heart rate <u>① increases</u>, your face becomes <u>② flushed</u>, and you may find yourself clenching your fists. These are signs that your body is preparing for a fight. But fighting is <u>③ always</u> the answer. Instead, try some first aid techniques to <u>④ calm</u> yourself down.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 '거의 ~이 아니다(rarely)'인데, '항상(always)'으로 바뀌었다. 싸움은 거의 답이 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① increases: 증가하다, 원문 일치
✅ ② flushed: 상기된, 원문 일치
❌ ③ always(항상) → rarely(거의 ~않다): 반의어로 교체됨
✅ ④ calm: 진정시키다, 원문 일치
det.tip: rarely(거의 ~않다) ↔ always(항상). 싸우는 것은 '거의' 답이 아니다.

questions.passage: Remember, everyone gets angry sometimes. It is a normal part of being human. But you have the power to choose how you respond to your anger. Don't let anger be your boss. Instead, learn to be the boss of your feelings. By understanding your anger, asking the right questions, calming yourself down, and finding proper coping skills, you can take control of your emotions and handle difficult situations in a <u>① healthier</u> way. All of these <u>② factors</u> can <u>③ diminish</u> feelings of anger. The key is to learn how to <u>④ manage</u> your anger.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 이 모든 요인들이 분노 감정에 '기여한다(contribute to)'인데, '줄이다(diminish)'로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① healthier: 더 건강한, 원문 일치
✅ ② factors: 요인들, 원문 일치
❌ ③ diminish(줄이다) → contribute to(기여하다): 요인들은 분노를 줄이는 것이 아니라 분노 감정에 기여한다
✅ ④ manage: 관리하다, 원문 일치
det.tip: contribute to(~에 기여하다) ↔ diminish(줄이다). 청소년기의 변화 요인들이 분노 감정에 '기여'한다는 맥락.

questions.passage: As a teenager, you are going through a lot of changes. You are developing your identity and trying to become __________. At the same time, your brain is still growing and is not yet fully developed.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 청소년기에 정체성을 발달시키고 독립적(independent)이 되려고 노력한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ independent: 독립적인, 원문 일치 — 정체성 발달과 독립 추구가 청소년기 특징
❌ ① dependent: 의존적인, 반의어
❌ ② popular: 인기 있는, 문맥 부적절
❌ ④ emotional: 감정적인, 문맥 부적절
det.tip: independent(독립적인) — 청소년기의 핵심 발달 과제 중 하나.

questions.passage: The part of your brain that controls emotions is more active than the part that controls __________ thinking. On top of that, hormones can make your emotions feel more intense than they really are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 감정을 통제하는 뇌 부분이 이성적(rational) 사고를 통제하는 부분보다 더 활발하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① rational: 이성적인, 원문 일치 — 감정 vs 이성의 대비 구조
❌ ② creative: 창의적인, 문맥 부적절
❌ ③ emotional: 감정적인, 앞부분과 중복
❌ ④ abstract: 추상적인, 문맥 부적절
det.tip: rational(이성적인) — 감정(emotions)과 대비되는 개념. 청소년 뇌에서 감정 영역이 이성 영역보다 활발하다.

questions.passage: Instead of focusing on how angry you feel, try to focus on finding a __________ to the problem that caused your anger. Remember, everyone gets angry sometimes. It is a normal part of being human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 분노를 느끼는 것에 집중하지 말고, 분노의 원인이 된 문제에 대한 해결책(solution)을 찾는 데 집중하라.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ solution: 해결책, 원문 일치 — problem-solving 기술의 핵심
❌ ① complaint: 불평, 건설적이지 않은 접근
❌ ② excuse: 변명, 문맥 부적절
❌ ③ punishment: 처벌, 문맥 부적절
det.tip: solution(해결책) — problem-solving(문제 해결)의 핵심. 분노의 감정이 아니라 원인 문제를 해결하는 데 집중해야 한다.

questions.passage: All of these factors can <u>contribute</u> to feelings of anger. Anger is a natural emotion, and it is not always a bad thing.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 contribute와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 이 모든 요인들이 분노 감정에 기여한다(contribute to).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ lead (to): ~에 이르게 하다, contribute to와 유사한 의미
❌ ① prevent: 예방하다, 반의어
❌ ② reduce: 줄이다, 반의어
❌ ④ respond: 반응하다, 다른 의미
det.tip: contribute to = lead to: ~에 기여하다, ~을 초래하다.

questions.passage: When you feel angry, it can be helpful to ask yourself some questions. These questions can help you step back and think more <u>clearly</u> before you act.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 clearly와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 행동하기 전에 한 발 물러서서 더 명확하게(clearly) 생각하게 해준다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② rationally: 이성적으로, clearly와 유사 — 분노 상황에서 명확한 사고는 이성적 사고를 의미
❌ ① vaguely: 모호하게, 반의어
❌ ③ emotionally: 감정적으로, 문맥 반대
❌ ④ quickly: 빠르게, 다른 의미
det.tip: clearly(명확하게) ≈ rationally(이성적으로). 분노 관리 맥락에서 명확한 사고 = 이성적 사고.

questions.passage: Once you have calmed down, it is important to find healthy ways to <u>deal with</u> your anger. Some people find it helpful to go for a walk or exercise.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 deal with와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 분노를 다루는(deal with) 건강한 방법을 찾는 것이 중요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① cope with: 대처하다, deal with의 동의어
❌ ② give up on: 포기하다, 다른 의미
❌ ③ run away from: 도망치다, 다른 의미
❌ ④ be proud of: 자랑스러워하다, 다른 의미
det.tip: deal with = cope with = handle: 다루다, 대처하다.

questions.passage: You are developing your identity and trying to become <u>independent</u>. At the same time, your brain is still growing and is not yet fully developed.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 independent와 의미가 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: 독립적(independent)이 되려고 노력한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② dependent: 의존적인, independent의 반의어
❌ ① self-reliant: 자립적인, 동의어
❌ ③ autonomous: 자율적인, 동의어
❌ ④ free: 자유로운, 유사 의미
det.tip: independent(독립적인) ↔ dependent(의존적인). self-reliant, autonomous는 동의어.

questions.passage: The key is to learn how to manage your anger in a <u>productive</u> way so that it does not control you.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 productive와 의미가 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: 분노를 생산적인(productive) 방식으로 관리하는 것이 핵심이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ destructive: 파괴적인, productive의 반의어
❌ ① constructive: 건설적인, 동의어
❌ ② effective: 효과적인, 유사 의미
❌ ③ useful: 유용한, 유사 의미
det.tip: productive(생산적인) ↔ destructive(파괴적인). constructive, effective, useful은 유사어.

questions.passage: But you have the <u>power</u> to choose how you respond to your anger. Don't let anger be your boss. Instead, learn to be the boss of your feelings.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 power와 같은 의미로 사용된 것은?
ch: The power went out during the storm.
Nuclear power is used in many countries.
You have the power to change your future.

det.korean: 당신은 분노에 대해 어떻게 반응할지 선택할 수 있는 능력(power)을 가지고 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ power to change: 능력/힘 (본문과 같은 의미)
❌ ① power went out: 전력 (정전)
❌ ② Nuclear power: 동력/에너지
❌ ④ horsepower: 마력 (기계적 출력)
det.tip: power: ① 전력 ② 동력/에너지 ③ 능력/권한 ④ 마력. 본문에서는 ③의 의미.

questions.passage: When anger hits, your body reacts physically. Your heart <u>rate</u> increases, your face becomes flushed, and you may find yourself clenching your fists.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 rate와 같은 의미로 사용된 것은?
ch: The crime rate in this area has decreased.
How would you rate this movie on a scale of 1 to 10?
We offer a special rate for students.
At this rate, we'll never finish on time.

det.korean: 분노가 몰려올 때 심장 박동수(heart rate)가 증가한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① crime rate: 범죄율/비율 (본문의 rate = 비율/속도와 같은 의미)
❌ ② rate this movie: 평가하다 (동사)
❌ ③ special rate: 요금
❌ ④ at this rate: 이런 속도로 (관용구)
det.tip: rate: ① 비율/속도 ② 평가하다 ③ 요금. heart rate = 심박수(비율/속도의 의미).

questions.passage: The part of your brain that controls emotions is more active than the part that controls rational thinking. On top of that, hormones can make your emotions feel more intense than they really are. All of these factors can contribute to __________(feel) of anger.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: 이 모든 요인들이 분노의 감정(feelings)에 기여할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ feelings: feel(느끼다)의 명사형 복수 — contribute to 뒤에 명사가 와야 하며, 여러 종류의 감정이므로 복수형
❌ feel: 동사 원형, 전치사 to 뒤에 부적절
❌ feeling: 단수형, 원문은 feelings 복수
❌ felt: 과거형, 문맥 부적절
det.tip: feel(동사: 느끼다) → feeling(명사: 감정) → feelings(복수형). contribute to + 명사 구조.

questions.passage: You are developing your identity and trying to become independent. At the same time, your brain is still growing and is not yet __________(full) developed.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: 뇌가 아직 완전히(fully) 발달하지 않았다.
det.analysis:
✅ fully: full(가득 찬)의 부사형 — developed(과거분사/형용사)를 수식해야 하므로 부사 필요
❌ full: 형용사, 형용사/과거분사를 수식할 수 없음
❌ fullness: 명사(충만함), 문맥 부적절
det.tip: full(형용사: 가득 찬) → fully(부사: 완전히). 과거분사 developed를 수식하므로 부사형이 필요.

questions.passage: When anger hits, your body reacts physically. Your heart rate increases, your face becomes flushed, and you may find yourself clenching your fists. These are signs that your body is preparing for __________. But fighting is rarely the answer.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이것들은 몸이 싸움(a fight)에 대비하고 있다는 신호이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② a fight: 싸움, 원문 일치 — 심박수 증가, 얼굴 상기, 주먹 쥐기 등은 싸움 준비 반응
❌ ① a celebration: 축하, 문맥 부적절
❌ ③ a conversation: 대화, 문맥 부적절
❌ ④ a rest: 휴식, 문맥 반대
det.tip: a fight(싸움) — 분노 시 신체 반응(심박수↑, 얼굴 상기, 주먹 쥐기)은 투쟁-도피 반응(fight-or-flight response).

questions.passage: Don't let anger be your boss. Instead, learn to be the boss of your feelings. By understanding your anger, asking the right questions, calming yourself down, and finding proper __________, you can take control of your emotions and handle difficult situations in a healthier way.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 적절한 대처 기술(coping skills)을 찾아 감정을 통제하고 어려운 상황을 더 건강하게 다룰 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ coping skills: 대처 기술, 원문 일치 — 글의 마지막 섹션 제목이자 핵심 개념
❌ ① excuses: 변명, 문맥 부적절
❌ ② distractions: 방해 요소, 문맥 부적절
❌ ③ complaints: 불평, 문맥 부적절
det.tip: coping skills(대처 기술) — 본문의 핵심 주제. 분노를 건강하게 관리하는 구체적 방법들.
